facts.fact_text: On 28 March 2006 a funeral of four militants of the PKK (Kurdish Workers' Party), an illegal armed organisation, took place in Diyarbakır.
On 28 March 2006 at around 7 a.m., the remains of the four PKK militants were taken to a mosque where around 1,500–2,000 people had gathered.
The crowd on 28 March 2006 walked to a cemetery for the burial of the four deceased PKK militants.
On 5 March 2007 a demonstration was held on the campus of Dicle University to protest about the conditions of Abdullah Öcalan's detention.
On 5 March 2007 the group of forty people held a press conference on the premises of Dicle University.
On 5 March 2007 the group of forty people chanted slogans in favour of the PKK and Abdullah Öcalan on the premises of Dicle University.
The applicant accepted to the Diyarbakır public prosecutor that he had participated in the funeral of one of the PKK militants on 28 March 2006.
The applicant stated to the Diyarbakır public prosecutor that on 5 March 2007 he had stood in front of the Dicle University building with other students for a short while.
In the first police video recording, the applicant was seen in a crowd next to a coffin making a 'V' sign.
In the third police video recording, the applicant was seen applauding with other students.
At the first hearing on 19 June 2007, the applicant stated that he had briefly participated in the gathering at Dicle University on 5 March 2007.
At the first hearing on 19 June 2007, the applicant accepted that he was the person in the photographs submitted as evidence.

The Diyarbakır Assize Court observed, on the basis of the police video recordings and photographs extracted from those recordings, that the applicant had attended the funeral of four PKK militants on 28 March 2006.
The Diyarbakır Assize Court observed that the applicant had walked in front of one of the coffins during the funeral of 28 March 2006.
On 9 March 2007 the applicant was arrested.

The judge of the Diyarbakır Assize Court remanded the applicant in custody on the basis of a strong suspicion that he had committed the offence of disseminating propaganda in support of a terrorist organisation or its purposes.

On 30 November 2007, at the end of the fourth hearing, the Diyarbakır Assize Court convicted the applicant of membership of an illegal organisation, the PKK, pursuant to Article 314 § 2 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 6 and 314 § 3 of the same Code.
The Diyarbakır Assize Court sentenced the applicant to six years and three months' imprisonment for membership of an illegal organisation, the PKK.
The Diyarbakır Assize Court convicted the applicant of two counts of disseminating propaganda in support of the PKK under section 7(2) of Law no. 3713.

The Diyarbakır Assize Court sentenced the applicant to a total of one year and eight months' imprisonment for two counts of disseminating propaganda in support of the PKK under section 7(2) of Law no. 3713.
The applicant was charged with disseminating propaganda in support of the PKK under section 7(2) of the Prevention of Terrorism Act (Law no. 3713).
The applicant was charged with membership of an illegal organisation under Article 314 § 2 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 6 and 314 § 3 of the same Code.

At the material time, Article 220 § 1 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) provided that anyone who establishes or directs organisations for the purpose of criminal activity shall be liable to imprisonment of between two and six years, provided that the structure of the organisation, the number of the members, and the quantity of the equipment and supplies are sufficient to commit the intended crimes.

At the material time, Article 220 § 2 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) provided that anyone who becomes a member of an organisation established for the purpose of criminal activity shall be liable to imprisonment of between one and three years.

At the material time, Article 220 § 6 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) provided that anyone who commits a crime on behalf of an illegal organisation, even if they are not a member of that organisation, shall also be punished for being a member of the organisation.

Article 314 § 2 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) provides that anyone who becomes a member of an armed organisation mentioned in Article 314 § 1 shall be liable to a term of imprisonment of between five and ten years.

At the material time, section 7(2) of the Prevention of Terrorism Act (Law no. 3713) provided that any person who disseminates propaganda in support of a terrorist organisation shall be liable to a term of imprisonment of between one and five years.
On 28 March 2006 a funeral of four militants of the PKK (Kurdish Workers' Party), an illegal armed organisation, took place in Diyarbakır.
The crowd at the mosque on 28 March 2006 chanted separatist, hostile slogans in Turkish and Kurdish in support of the PKK and Abdullah Öcalan, the leader of the PKK.
The crowd at the mosque on 28 March 2006 waved PKK posters and banners.
After being warned by the police on 28 March 2006, the crowd became agitated and started throwing stones at the police officers on duty, injuring a number of them.
The crowd on 28 March 2006 caused extensive damage to State buildings and vehicles, banks, shops, and other vehicles belonging to private individuals.
The applicant was charged with disseminating propaganda in support of the PKK under section 7(2) of the Prevention of Terrorism Act (Law no. 3713).
The applicant was charged with membership of an illegal organisation under Article 314 § 2 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237), on the basis of Articles 220 § 6 and 314 § 3 of the same Code.
The applicant accepted to the Diyarbakır public prosecutor that he had participated in the funeral of one of the PKK militants on 28 March 2006.
The applicant stated to the Diyarbakır public prosecutor that the PKK militant whose funeral he attended on 28 March 2006 had been a relative of a friend of his.
The applicant stated to the Diyarbakır public prosecutor that he had attended the funeral on 28 March 2006 as a religious duty.
The applicant stated to the Diyarbakır public prosecutor that he had not attacked the police with stones during the events of 28 March 2006.
The applicant stated to the Diyarbakır public prosecutor that on 5 March 2007 he had stood in front of the Dicle University building with other students for a short while.
The applicant stated to the Diyarbakır public prosecutor that he had not chanted slogans with the demonstrators on 5 March 2007.
In the first police video recording, the applicant was seen in a crowd next to a coffin making a 'V' sign.
In the third police video recording, the applicant was seen applauding with other students.
At the first hearing on 19 June 2007, the applicant denied the accuracy of the allegation that he had chanted slogans during the funeral of 28 March 2006.
At the first hearing on 19 June 2007, the applicant denied the accuracy of the allegation that he had chanted slogans during the demonstration of 5 March 2007.
At the first hearing on 19 June 2007, the applicant stated that he did not remember making a 'V' sign but that he might have done so along with the rest of the crowd.
The Diyarbakır Assize Court observed that the applicant had made a 'V' sign during the funeral of 28 March 2006.
The Diyarbakır Assize Court noted that it was not established that the applicant had chanted slogans during the funeral of 28 March 2006.

The Diyarbakır Assize Court noted that during the demonstration held on 5 March 2007 at Dicle University, the applicant had applauded while other demonstrators chanted slogans in support of Abdullah Öcalan.

The Diyarbakır Assize Court found it established that the applicant had acted with the intention of supporting the deceased PKK militants on 28 March 2006, thereby committing the offence of disseminating propaganda in favour of the PKK and its leader.

The Diyarbakır Assize Court found it established that the applicant had acted together with illegal demonstrators on 5 March 2007, thereby committing the offence of disseminating propaganda in favour of the PKK and its leader.

The Diyarbakır Assize Court considered that the applicant's participation in the funeral and demonstration of 28 March 2006 and his conduct at that time had occurred as a result of instructions and calls by the PKK.
The Diyarbakır Assize Court considered that the applicant had acted on behalf of the PKK, in line with the goals and activities of the PKK.
The Diyarbakır Assize Court considered that the applicant should be punished not only for disseminating propaganda but also for membership of an illegal organisation.

The dissenting judge stated that neither Article 220 § 6 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) nor the explanatory memorandum on Article 220 § 6 explained the concept of committing an offence on behalf of an illegal organisation.

The dissenting judge noted that an offence committed on behalf of an illegal organisation should be capable of producing a result for a terrorist organisation and its aims, such as the offences of aggravated injury, kidnapping, deprivation of liberty, murder or bombing.

The dissenting judge noted that an offence committed on behalf of an illegal organisation should have devastating repercussions for society when the way of committing the offence, the time of the offence and its effects were taken into consideration.

The dissenting judge opined that in order to conclude that non-members of an illegal organisation had committed an offence on behalf of that illegal organisation, there should be a decision to commit an offence on behalf of that organisation and an intention to join the organisation in question.
The dissenting judge concluded that the applicant should only have been convicted under section 7(2) of Law no. 3713 (the Prevention of Terrorism Act).

The Plenary Court of Cassation (Criminal Divisions) of Turkey held on 4 March 2008 that participation in unauthorised demonstrations held after appeals by an illegal organisation and acts which constituted independent offences committed during those demonstrations could be considered as having been carried out on behalf of the organisation.

The Plenary Court of Cassation (Criminal Divisions) of Turkey held on 4 March 2008 that such acts should be sanctioned under Article 314 § 2 of the Criminal Code (Law no. 5237) on the basis of Articles 220 § 6 and 314 § 3, along with other criminal-law provisions.

The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 noted that acts such as 'participating in a public demonstration following a general call from pro-PKK media outlets, making victory sign and shouting slogans to support and in favour of the leader of a terrorist organisation, clashing with the security forces and forming barricades' are considered crimes committed on behalf of an organisation and not as membership.

The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 stated that the expression of an opinion in its different forms should not be the only evidence before domestic courts to decide on the membership of the defendant in an armed organisation.

The Venice Commission's Opinion CDL-AD(2016)002 stated that where the only evidence consists of forms of expression, a conviction for being a member of an armed organisation would constitute an interference with the right of the defendants to freedom of expression, and that the necessity of this interference should be examined in the concrete circumstances of each case on the basis of the criteria set forth in the case-law of the ECtHR, in particular the criterion of 'incitement to violence'.

Mr Thomas Hammarberg stated in his report of 10 January 2012 that the provisions contained in the Turkish anti-terror legislation and Article 220 of the Criminal Code of Turkey allow for a very wide margin of appreciation, in particular in cases where membership in a terrorist organisation has not been proven and when an act or statement may be deemed to coincide with the aims or instructions of a terrorist organisation.
